name: Apartheid
summary: Apartheid was the doctrine and legal system of racial separation under National Party rule in South Africa from 1948 to 1994. It treated South Africa as several distinct peoples, kept political power with the white minority under the idea of guardianship, and justified separate development and homelands as good for every group. It combined Afrikaner nationalism, claimed Christian grounds, strong anti-communism, and a security state.
scope: The official National Party ideology of 1948-1990, centred on H.F. Verwoerd's 'separate development' and the laws of 1949-1959 (race classification, group areas, mixed-marriage bans, Bantu Education, homelands). It excludes post-1990 reform and later uses of the word for other systems.

universal-healthcare.rationale: Inferred: services were provided in racially unequal tiers, with white areas favoured, so a universal guarantee was not the aim.

raise-minimum-wage.rationale: Inferred: the economy relied on cheap Black migrant and rural labour, which a substantial wage rise would have undercut.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: Split: the state heavily directed where Black labour could live and work and steered industry to homelands, yet the economy stayed capitalist.

public-ownership.rationale: Nationalist governments did create state corporations, but ownership was never a defining issue for the doctrine.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: Inferred: white economic benefit was preserved by the system, and redistributive taxation was not part of its program.

unions-good.rationale: Black unions were unrecognised and organisations such as SACTU were banned under anti-communist legislation, while white labour was protected.

property-fundamental.rationale: Whites owned almost all industrial and agricultural land and Black land rights were restricted, so property was protected for the ruling group, though the state overrode Black holdings freely.

regulate-corporations.rationale: Business was regulated for racial ends (permits, industrial decentralisation), but not for general public-interest reasons.

cut-welfare.rationale: Welfare was generous for whites and minimal for Blacks; adherents had no single line on cutting it.

worker-ownership.rationale: Inferred: collective worker ownership belongs to the socialism the National Party fought as communism.

surveillance-ok.rationale: The regime used banning orders, security police and emergency powers against suspected subversives as routine security policy.

legalize-drugs.rationale: Inferred from the conservative moral order and heavy policing of the regime; not addressed in sources.

restrict-hate-speech.rationale: Speech laws were used to silence opponents rather than to protect racial groups from hate; the doctrine itself rested on racial hierarchy.

strong-leader.rationale: Verwoerd urged following strong leaders who will not cave in, and the system was an authoritarian political culture.

state-harmful.rationale: Apartheid was built on a powerful state classifying, relocating and policing citizens, so the claim that the state is harmful is opposed to its whole machinery.

limit-guns.rationale: White civilians were generally armed in the militarised society, while Black people were disarmed; no unified position on limits.

empower-police-military.rationale: The Total Strategy built up a large military and counter-intelligence apparatus, and security forces were given sweeping powers after Sharpeville.

legalize-sex-work.rationale: Inferred: the regime policed sexual morality, including the Immorality Acts, and was conservative on sexual matters.

decide-locally.rationale: Power was centralised in the white national government; homeland self-government was ethnic, not a local-decision principle.

rehabilitation.rationale: Inferred: security and punishment, including hanging for treason, characterised the system.

traditional-family.rationale: Family and sexual law policed racial boundaries and the movement was socially conservative, with Afrikaner Christian family values.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: The Calvinist, conservative Afrikaner establishment and its state opposed it; the sources do not discuss it directly.

abortion-legal.rationale: Inferred from the Christian-national conservatism of the movement; not stated in sources.

more-religion-public.rationale: Verwoerd linked white hegemony and the victory of Christianity and invoked a God-given destination for whites in Africa.

correct-racial-injustice.rationale: The doctrine denied that racial hierarchy was an injustice and presented separation as justice; it would reject remedial action as an assault on white interests.

gender-social-construct.rationale: Inferred: the system was built on fixed natural differences between racial groups and a conservative view of gender.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: The principle of one volk, one state, with schools serving the ethnic group and the people's ideal as the highest aim, makes cultural preservation central.

gradual-change.rationale: Verwoerd saw progress as inevitable and planned, but he also defended the existing order against rapid change.

reduce-immigration.rationale: White immigration was encouraged in some periods while Black movement was controlled by pass laws; no uniform stance.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: South Africa left the Commonwealth in 1961 rather than accept criticism of racism, and rejected outside interference in its racial policy.

free-trade.rationale: Economic policy was pragmatic and state-managed, with sanctions as a pressure; no doctrine on free trade.

nation-first.rationale: Verwoerd built a siege mentality and left the Commonwealth to protect Afrikaner and white interests ahead of international standing.

humanitarian-intervention.rationale: Apartheid rejected outside interference in its internal affairs, though it carried out its own cross-border military operations.

open-borders.rationale: Pass laws, group areas and homeland citizenship were all instruments for controlling who could be where.

limit-growth.rationale: Inferred: the regime was pro-industrial development; environmental limits were not an issue.

drastic-climate-action.rationale: Inferred: no stated position; the movement was pro-industry and conservative.

tech-solves-problems.rationale: Verwoerd had a belief in inevitable progress, but no doctrine on technology as the solver of problems.

expand-nuclear.rationale: South Africa pursued nuclear capability and a self-reliant security strategy, though this was not an ideological claim.

revolution-justified.rationale: The state banned the ANC and PAC and treated revolutionary opposition as terrorism and communism to be crushed.

experts-over-public.rationale: Verwoerd was a rationalist who relied on planning, yet the franchise restricted to whites was seen as a popular basis within the volk.

central-planning.rationale: Inferred: state direction of racial geography existed, but a planned economy was associated with communism, which was opposed.

socialized-markets.rationale: Inferred: public or worker ownership belongs to the socialist tradition the regime opposed.

land-value-tax.rationale: Not addressed in any source consulted; no clear adherent position.

tax-inheritance.rationale: Inferred from protection of white property and wealth; not addressed in sources.

basic-income.rationale: Inferred: unconditional transfers fit neither the labour system nor the racially tiered welfare structure.

tariffs-protect-industry.rationale: Inferred from the state-directed industrial policy, including steering industry to the homelands by law.

state-directs-investment.rationale: The 1959 Bantu Investment Corporation Act and a 1967 law let the government redirect industrial development to homeland borders.

widespread-small-property.rationale: White farm ownership was favoured; wide distribution of property was applied only within racial limits.

abolish-money-wages.rationale: The migrant-labour economy depended on wage labour; abolishing it is communist, and communism was banned.

abolish-central-banks.rationale: Inferred: no sign of any such position among adherents.

corporatist-bargaining.rationale: The system recognised white labour structures but not Black ones; no clear corporatist doctrine.

one-party-rule.rationale: The National Party dominated the white parliamentary system, but there were rival white parties until late; not a stated single-party doctrine.

monarchy-legitimate.rationale: Verwoerd pursued a republic as the form of the people's government, and rejected British monarchy.

democracy-best.rationale: Political rights were denied to the Black majority; democracy was justified only within the white or ethnic group.

direct-votes.rationale: Inferred: referendums were used only for key constitutional questions such as the republic.

workers-councils.rationale: Soviet-type organisation was denounced as communist and banned under the Suppression of Communism Act.

right-to-secede.rationale: The state would not allow Black groups to leave except through approved homelands, while white domination was kept at the centre.

natural-rulers.rationale: Verwoerd held that whites and Blacks were on different levels and that whites should keep guardianship and hegemony.

political-violence-never.rationale: The state itself used lethal force and the Total Strategy included cross-border strikes, so it did not hold that violence is never justified.

war-builds-character.rationale: Militarised society, but the specific claim was not made central to doctrine.

separate-church-state.rationale: Verwoerd tied Christianity's victory to white hegemony and the state, and the Dutch Reformed Church backed the policy.

laws-from-scripture.rationale: Verwoerd did not take specific Christian beliefs as a basis for political action, even if he claimed faith backed policy.

private-courts-defense.rationale: Inferred: security was a state matter in the militarised state.

military-superiority.rationale: Total Strategy built a large conventional military in response to perceived Soviet and African threats.

ethnic-nation.rationale: The government held that South Africa was composed of distinct nations, and each should have its own political home.

class-struggle-history.rationale: The regime saw communism as the enemy and defined opposition as communist; it saw race and volk as the primary categories, not class.

equal-outcomes.rationale: Benefits were deliberately concentrated on whites, and the system explicitly rejected equality among groups.

indigenous-land-authority.rationale: Land was set aside in homelands for Black groups (about 13 percent), but this was ethnic reservation, not indigenous authority.

colonial-reparations.rationale: Verwoerd stated that whites brought civilisation and that Blacks owed what they had to it, so there was no debt.

civilizational-union.rationale: Verwoerd linked the white man in Africa to the struggle of the white man of Europe and America to keep his hegemony.

self-interest-moral.rationale: Verwoerd demanded sacrifice for the volk's ideal, which cuts against individual self-interest as such.

duties-before-rights.rationale: Rights and justice were recognised only within the ethnic community, with sacrifice for the volk demanded above all else.

nature-intrinsic-value.rationale: Not addressed in sources and not a doctrinal matter.

limit-population.rationale: The state was concerned about Black population growth but this was not a framed doctrine.

industrial-civilization-disaster.rationale: Inferred: the regime was pro-industry and wanted growth and white prosperity.

accelerate-technology.rationale: Inferred: the regime defended an established order.

human-enhancement.rationale: Inferred from a conservative moral outlook; not addressed.

algorithmic-government.rationale: Not addressed; anachronistic, and inferred from the conservative outlook.

unbreakable-encryption.rationale: Inferred from the regime's heavy surveillance and security-state orientation.

restore-past-order.rationale: Defended an existing racial order, not a lost one.

results-over-ideology.rationale: Verwoerd followed rigid axioms rationally applied, rather than pragmatic results.

direct-action.rationale: The system suppressed direct-action campaigns such as the Defiance Campaign with mass arrests and bans.

means-match-ends.rationale: Inferred: the system used coercion for its goal of separation.

return-to-foraging.rationale: Inferred: no sign of any such position.

abolish-division-of-labor.rationale: The racially defined division of labour was central to the system.

distribute-by-need.rationale: The doctrine concentrated benefits on whites and condemned communism.

production-for-use.rationale: Capitalist production for profit continued, and socialism was suppressed.

profit-exploitation.rationale: The regime condemned communism and denied any Marxist analysis; profit was normal.

dictatorship-of-proletariat.rationale: The Suppression of Communism Act banned the Communist Party and its aims, and the government pledged to purge communist sympathisers.

collective-farming.rationale: Communism-linked collectivism was anathema; white-owned farms were private.

capitalism-causes-war.rationale: A Marxist reading was rejected by a regime defining itself against communism.

taxation-theft.rationale: Not a stated principle; the state was strong and taxed.

harm-principle.rationale: The state restricted adults' conduct widely, from sex to association.

individual-rights-only.rationale: Verwoerd recognised justice and rights chiefly as those of each people, not of individuals.

conscription.rationale: The state maintained white conscription to defend the Total Strategy.

exit-over-voice.rationale: Inferred: rejected, since pass laws restricted movement of Black people.

state-as-business.rationale: Not a doctrinal matter; inferred from authoritarian statism.

positive-liberty.rationale: Inferred from lack of social provision for the majority.

media-academia-power.rationale: Press and universities were censored, but the claim is not a core doctrine.

hereditarian-race.rationale: Verwoerd saw Blacks as of vastly lesser capabilities, and the Population Registration Act sorted people by ancestry and appearance.

organic-representation.rationale: Verwoerd conceived of the people in organic terms, and of representation within each volk.

total-state.rationale: Education was to serve the ethnic group, a totalitarian approach in Venter's reading, but the doctrine did not call for state direction of every area of life.

national-rebirth.rationale: Verwoerd's vision was progress to a destined triumph, rather than rebirth from decadence.

territorial-expansion.rationale: The policy was homelands and separation; South West Africa was held, but the doctrine did not centre on expansion.

personal-loyalty-rule.rationale: Inferred: modern republic form, not feudal fealty.

bound-labor.rationale: Pass laws and influx control tied Black labour to designated places and permits, in effect restricting labour mobility.

no-neutral-knowledge.rationale: Verwoerd was a rationalist trusting logic from axioms, in contrast to relativism.

universal-morality.rationale: Verwoerd's moral claims were bound to ethnic community, though he invoked a common basis of humanness.

single-common-good.rationale: Verwoerd's ideal subordinated competing interests to the volk's ideal, but the common good was group-bounded.

jewish-state-israel.rationale: South Africa later had ties with Israel, but this was not a doctrine of apartheid.

revive-national-language.rationale: Afrikaans was promoted as an official language, with the 1974 Afrikaans Medium Decree, but the revival frame does not fit.

workplace-democracy.rationale: Black unions were not recognised, and management control was not shared.

school-vouchers.rationale: The state ran a centralised racial education system under Bantu Education.

economic-freedom.rationale: Business freedom was valued but the system sharply restricted Black economic freedom.

rule-by-example.rationale: The system relied on laws and punishments.

national-self-determination.rationale: The justification for homelands was that each nation should govern itself, with Verwoerd promoting separation into multiple ethno-states.

force-without-un.rationale: South Africa ran cross-border operations such as Protea and Askari in defiance of international condemnation.

reason-over-faith.rationale: Verwoerd was a rationalist who also claimed a God-given destination.

welfare-for-citizens.rationale: Homeland citizenship stripped Black people of South African citizenship, limiting their claim on state provision.

class-collaboration.rationale: The state opposed class struggle ideology; the white nation was to work together across language divides.

sacrifice-heritage.rationale: Inferred: heritage preservation was central to the movement.

dominated-front.rationale: South Africa saw itself aligned with the West against communism.

workers-nation.rationale: Inferred: labour organised along ethnic lines fit the policy.

distinct-gender-roles.rationale: Inferred: conservative social order; the sources do not discuss gender.

ban-interest.rationale: Inferred: capitalist economy with ordinary banking.

racial-segregation-law.rationale: The Population Registration and Group Areas Acts classified people by race and restricted where they could live, and separate facilities were mandated by law.

state-class-instrument.rationale: The state's self-presentation was as guardian of the volk and the white nation, not a class tool; Marxism was banned.

expand-fossil-fuels.rationale: South Africa expanded coal and synthetic fuel for self-reliance under sanctions; inferred.

assimilate-immigrants.rationale: Verwoerd wanted unity of Afrikaans and English whites into one volk; non-white assimilation was refused.

elite-replacement.rationale: Not a doctrine, though the fear of white swamping was present.

proportional-representation.rationale: Inferred: the white-only franchise used constituency voting.

national-mission.rationale: Verwoerd saw a God-given destination in Africa for whites, but not a mission to spread governance to others.

patriarchy-structural.rationale: Inferred from a conservative outlook; not stated.

political-elite-corrupt.rationale: Verwoerd demanded loyalty to the volk's government and treated disloyalty as treason.

security-forces-accountable.rationale: Security forces were shielded and the Truth Commission era only followed the end of the system.

night-watchman-state.rationale: The system was highly interventionist, planning race, residence, education and labour.

discourage-race-mixing.rationale: Mixed marriage and cross-racial sex were barred in 1949-50 laws, and the National Party stood against mixing of blood.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: Verwoerd admitted a common basis of humanness but held Blacks to have vastly lesser capabilities and that equal rights did not follow.

settler-state-colonial.rationale: Verwoerd held that white men brought civilisation and that God planted Afrikaners in Africa with a destination.

uniform-civil-code.rationale: The system maintained distinct legal treatment by race group, including race-specific marriage and residence law.

ban-cattle-slaughter.rationale: Inferred: no sign of any such position.

no-religion-state-schools.rationale: Christian National Education shaped white schools, though sources used here do not discuss it in detail.

state-strengthens-encirclement.rationale: Not a socialist context, though the state saw itself as encircled.

consent-of-governed.rationale: Political rights were denied to the Black majority, so authority rested on the white electorate only.

population-transfer.rationale: Between 1960 and 1983, 3.5 million Black South Africans were forcibly removed, and homeland citizenship stripped them of South African citizenship.

initiating-force-wrong.rationale: The state used force against opponents and neighbours as policy.

competition-drives-progress.rationale: Not addressed; the ideology stressed each people's survival.

ban-extremist-parties.rationale: The Suppression of Communism Act banned the Communist Party and any party with similar aims, and the ANC and PAC were banned after Sharpeville.

freedom-as-non-domination.rationale: The system placed the Black majority under the arbitrary control of white officials through permits and boards.

separated-powers.rationale: Parliament was supreme under the white franchise, with courts occasionally resisting; no doctrine.

vanguard-party.rationale: A Leninist model was among the targets of anti-communist laws.

priority-to-poor.rationale: State benefits favoured whites, and a priority to the poor was not part of the doctrine.

restrict-strikes-picketing.rationale: Black strikes were illegal and unions were banned, so the state restricted labour action.

population-causes-poverty.rationale: Not addressed in the consulted sources.

diversity-weakens-cohesion.rationale: The foundation of the system was that integration caused loss of identity and clashes, per the Sauer Commission, so separation was needed.

offices-by-lottery.rationale: Inferred: no sign of any such position.

party-controls-media.rationale: Film, literature and media were censored under the Customs and Excise Act 1955 and the Official Secrets Act 1956, and mainstream media largely supported the system.

party-commands-army.rationale: The armed forces were under the state; party control was not formalised.

long-naturalization-wait.rationale: Citizenship was racially limited, and non-white access to it was withheld entirely.

party-discipline-binding.rationale: Verwoerd demanded loyalty and treated disloyalty to the volk as treachery.

pool-sovereignty.rationale: The republic and the exit from the Commonwealth show opposition to supranational authority.

head-commands-forces.rationale: The state president was ceremonial for most of the period; changed with 1984 constitution.

church-by-bishops.rationale: The Dutch Reformed Church had a synodal structure; no stated position.

clerical-rule.rationale: Verwoerd did not make clergy the political authority but backed the state's policy with faith.

defeat-own-government-war.rationale: Verwoerd treated anyone who did not serve his volk as a traitor.

censor-art-for-virtue.rationale: The Publications Control system censored film and literature on morals and political grounds.

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: South Africa had no formal alliance; this was not a stated issue.

abolish-rental-housing.rationale: Township rental housing was central to control of urban Black residents.

people-in-arms.rationale: White civilians were armed as part of commando structures, but a professional army existed.

rural-life-healthier.rationale: The homelands were meant to keep Black people in rural settings, and Afrikaner nationalism had a rural romance.

reunify-divided-nation.rationale: The policy divided the country into separate states.

cultures-equal-different.rationale: Verwoerd saw whites as bearers of civilisation, but also said each people should develop along its own lines.

death-penalty.rationale: Political offenders convicted of treason could be hanged.

sex-ed-in-schools.rationale: Inferred from a conservative moral order.

creationism-in-schools.rationale: Christian National Education shaped white schools, though not documented in sources used.

restrict-pornography.rationale: The censorship regime banned material under the Customs and Excise Act and a publications board.

citizenship-by-descent.rationale: Citizenship and homeland belonging followed ancestry and racial classification.

minority-language-support.rationale: Afrikaans and English were official languages, and homeland languages were supported at a different level.

encourage-eccentricity.rationale: Inferred from the conformist moral order enforced by law.

sovereign-debt-cancellation.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from a creditworthy capitalist stance.

independence-needs-economic-change.rationale: Inferred: the white-owned economy was to continue as before.

constituent-assembly.rationale: Constitutions were made by the white parliament, not an assembly of all people.

restrict-freedoms-for-growth.rationale: Inferred from the willingness to restrict freedoms to preserve order and prosperity.

independent-nuclear-deterrent.rationale: South Africa developed its own nuclear capability under the Total Strategy.

direct-election-head-of-state.rationale: Not addressed in sources; the head of state was chosen by parliament or electoral college in the white system.

central-bank-independence.rationale: Not addressed in the sources used.

no-land-for-peace.rationale: Inferred from the stance of holding territory and the siege mentality.

property-serves-common-good.rationale: Property rights were protected for the ruling group, though the state overrode Black holdings for the volk's goals.

soviet-state-capitalist.rationale: Apartheid thinkers saw the USSR as a communist enemy and did not use this analysis.

precautionary-principle.rationale: Inferred: not an issue for the movement.

collective-defense.rationale: The government warned of a Soviet threat to the Cape sea route and looked to Western security; formal alliances were absent.

annexed-territory-occupation.rationale: South Africa administered South West Africa as a colonial territory and rejected claims it was unlawful.

subordinate-church-to-state.rationale: The church and state were aligned in support of policy; Verwoerd saw faith as backing the government.

force-to-prevent-secession.rationale: Not addressed; homeland independence was state-granted.

region-keeps-system.rationale: Homelands were given self-government under white control, but this was not the same as the claim stated.

sacred-ruler.rationale: Verwoerd favoured a republic, not a sacred monarchy.

flat-income-tax.rationale: Not addressed in the sources used.

character-from-environment.rationale: The Population Registration Act sorted people by ancestry and appearance, treating racial group as a fixed category.

space-expansion.rationale: Inferred: not an issue for the doctrine.

leader-cult.rationale: Verwoerd demanded following strong leaders, though a leader cult in the sense of statues and mass praise is not documented.

class-struggle-under-socialism.rationale: Inferred: the regime rejected socialism wholesale.

land-redistribution.rationale: Whites owned almost all industrial and agricultural land, Blacks were allotted about 13 percent, and the government did not redistribute it to Black farmers.

refugee-return.rationale: Inferred: removals were enforced to separate groups.

apostasy-punishable.rationale: Not addressed; the Dutch Reformed tradition did not call for it.

kin-peoples-union.rationale: Not addressed; Afrikaner nationalism focused on a South African volk.

national-cultural-autonomy.rationale: The government held that each racial group should have its own institutions and schools, though with a state of its own as the aim for Black groups.

rights-where-you-live.rationale: Homeland policy aimed to move Black political rights out of South Africa proper.

material-conditions-drive-history.rationale: Verwoerd saw the volk's ideal and Christian destiny as drivers, not economics.

courts-bound-by-majority.rationale: Parliament was supreme for the white majority, and the government overrode court decisions with new laws.

gender-parity-bodies.rationale: Inferred: not an aim; conservative outlook.

economic-self-sufficiency.rationale: Sanctions pushed autarky later, but it was not a goal as a doctrine.

trade-labor-env-standards.rationale: Inferred: external demands were rejected as interference.

moral-incentives.rationale: Inferred: capitalist economy and racial rewards.

armed-group-creates-revolution.rationale: Revolutionary guerrilla action was the enemy that the security state fought.

abolish-hereditary-privilege.rationale: Not addressed, though racial status was inherited and privileged.

history-own-civilization.rationale: Education was conceived as serving the needs of the ethnic group with its own history and traditions.

civilizing-tutelage.rationale: The National Party stood for Christian guardianship of the white race over non-white peoples, to let them develop within their own context.

patriotic-education.rationale: Education was to serve the volk and the ethnic group, with loyalty to the people prized above all else.

end-racial-preferences.rationale: Inferred: it entrenched white preference itself, and would oppose reversal of it.

public-money-creation.rationale: Not addressed in the sources used.

capitalism-adapts.rationale: The regime relied on capitalist industry; inferred.

former-empire-influence.rationale: Not addressed; South Africa had influence in neighbouring territories.

labor-aristocracy.rationale: A Marxist concept not used by the movement.

freedom-to-discriminate.rationale: The system required discrimination by law in public life, so it did not see private freedom of association as the main point.

entrenched-bill-of-rights.rationale: Parliamentary sovereignty let the government pass race laws without any rights limit.

colonial-treaties-void.rationale: Inferred; the doctrine defended settler-era arrangements.

elective-rulers.rationale: Verwoerd favoured a republic with elected rulers for the white electorate.

minority-veto.rationale: Whites were a minority wishing to retain control, but no formal veto principle was stated.

resist-lawless-ruler.rationale: Verwoerd demanded loyalty to the volk's government.

parliament-supreme.rationale: Parliament passed the apartheid laws and no entrenched rights restricted it.

noblesse-oblige.rationale: The doctrine of white guardianship held that whites had a duty to look after and develop Black communities.

withdraw-from-politics.rationale: Verwoerd demanded sacrifice for the volk and treated those who did not serve it as traitors.

ruling-class-consent.rationale: Not a framework the doctrine used.

world-economy-extracts-surplus.rationale: The regime rejected the idea that South Africa's wealth came from exploitation; sanctions were seen as unjust.

native-born-offices.rationale: Not addressed; offices were reserved for whites.

party-own-road.rationale: A communist question, not addressed by this ideology.

self-reliance-over-aid.rationale: South Africa sought self-reliance under sanctions.

indigenous-political-leadership.rationale: Verwoerd held the white man brought civilisation and kept hegemony, rejecting Black political leadership over whites.

antifascism-founding-value.rationale: Inferred: the movement defined itself against communism and Afrikaner nationalism had no antifascist commitment in the sources used.

totalitarianisms-equivalent.rationale: Not addressed; the regime was anti-communist, but did not condemn fascism.

slavery-not-civil-war-cause.rationale: Not addressed; irrelevant to the doctrine.

preserve-contested-monuments.rationale: Preserving the volk's symbols and heritage was central, and condemnation from outside was dismissed.

institutions-fit-civilization.rationale: Verwoerd argued each people needed its own form of development and government, with separate states for each group.

military-guardian-role.rationale: The security establishment gained a large political role under Total Strategy.

filial-duty.rationale: Inferred from the conservative family values.

land-use-tenure.rationale: Whites held freehold land; tribal tenure applied in homelands.

budget-needs-parliament.rationale: The parliamentary system was kept for whites; inferred.

single-official-language.rationale: The state recognised Afrikaans and English as official languages and supported homeland languages in separate education.

disparate-impact-discrimination.rationale: The doctrine held that racially unequal outcomes were natural consequences of separate development, not discrimination.

arm-foreign-insurgents.rationale: Inferred from the cross-border operations such as Protea and Askari; arming insurgents is not described in the sources used.

restrict-foreign-funding.rationale: The state banned or restricted opponents and their foreign support under security laws.

residents-only-property.rationale: The Group Areas Act limited ownership and residence to designated groups.

democratic-peace.rationale: Inferred: democracy was limited to whites.

no-duty-to-obey.rationale: Verwoerd demanded loyalty and treated disloyal citizens as traitors.

non-intervention.rationale: Verwoerd said outside criticism was made in ignorance and that South Africa would act by its own judgement.

minority-conspiracy.rationale: Communists and liberals were cast as a conspiracy against the state.

abolish-legal-marriage.rationale: The state regulated marriage heavily by race, so it held marriage law central.

public-access-to-information.rationale: The Official Secrets Act 1956 and censorship restricted information.

national-law-over-international.rationale: South Africa rejected international condemnation and left the Commonwealth rather than accept limits on its racial policy.

religious-nation.rationale: Verwoerd's nation was ethnic and white Christian, but defined by volk more than religion.

regional-revenue-retention.rationale: Homelands were to be funded and developed separately; inferred.

personal-possessions-private.rationale: Private property was protected; communism was opposed.

defeat-communism.rationale: The Suppression of Communism Act and the pledge to purge communist sympathisers show the aim to defeat rather than coexist with communism.

religion-illusion.rationale: Verwoerd saw faith as a backing for his policy and Christianity's victory as a goal.

capitalism-progressive.rationale: Industry and capital were valued; inferred.

purge-loanwords.rationale: Not addressed; Afrikaans purism existed but was not central.

treaties-binding.rationale: Inferred; treaties with Black polities were not honoured.

majority-settlement.rationale: Group areas separated groups rather than placing majorities among minorities.

neither-capitalism-nor-communism.rationale: Capitalism continued as the economic basis, with communism the enemy.

historical-land-claim.rationale: Verwoerd held that God planted whites in Africa with a destination, a claim of right to the land.

holocaust-denial.rationale: Not a documented position of the ideology.

criminalize-homosexuality.rationale: Inferred from the socially conservative Afrikaner order; the sources used do not address same-sex relations.

suppress-opposition.rationale: Banning orders, the Suppression of Communism Act and the banning of the ANC and PAC after Sharpeville were used to silence opposition.

colonies-serve-metropole.rationale: South West Africa was administered as a colonial territory, and labour from the rural areas benefited whites.

participatory-democracy.rationale: Political rights were denied to the Black majority, with no participation allowed.

intersecting-oppressions.rationale: The doctrine denied that racial order was oppression.

gender-identity-recognition.rationale: Inferred from a conservative moral outlook.

left-right-obsolete.rationale: Verwoerd's axioms were ideological, and the movement was firmly on one side against communism.

emergency-suspend-protections.rationale: After Sharpeville the government declared a state of emergency and arrested more than 18,000 people, and banning orders suspended ordinary protections against suspected subversives.

price-controls-essentials.rationale: Not addressed in the sources used and no clear adherent position.

sovereign-above-law.rationale: Parliament was sovereign and made the racial laws, but a ruler above the law was not a stated claim.

alienated-labor.rationale: Inferred: the National Party was strongly anti-communist and defended a racially ordered capitalist economy.

islam-incompatible.rationale: Not addressed in the sources; apartheid classified Cape Malay Muslims as a separate group, and its Christian-nationalist ideology gave no settled position.

divine-source-of-authority.rationale: Apartheid ideology claimed Christian-national grounds and a divine calling for separate peoples, with state authority resting on that mandate.

religious-dress-in-state.rationale: Not addressed; schools were Christian-national and organized by race, and dress was not a stated issue.

ban-nda-harassment.rationale: Anachronistic; inferred from the regime's weak protection of workers' legal claims against employers.

social-market-economy.rationale: Split: the state ran large enterprises and racial protections for whites, but it did not guarantee social security across the population.

abolish-armed-forces.rationale: Apartheid South Africa was a security state that built up its military and police to defend white rule against internal and external threats.

rich-first.rationale: Inferred: separate development and the homelands were justified as stages in group development, while whites held the wealth and power first.

stay-neutral-between-blocs.rationale: Split: the regime was anti-communist and sought Western ties but wanted independence of action and was shunned by the West.

dynastic-succession.rationale: South Africa under the National Party was a republic from 1961 with an elected white legislature and a president chosen by it, so hereditary office had no place.

interest-free-mutual-credit.rationale: Inferred: the National Party state backed capitalism for whites, alongside Afrikaner mutual and state-backed finance, but not interest-free mutual banking.

refuse-lender-austerity.rationale: Inferred: the regime stressed national self-sufficiency and resisted outside pressure during sanctions, but the sources do not describe a stance on IMF conditions.

property-franchise.rationale: The franchise was limited by race, not property; the Cape's older qualified franchise was abolished for Africans and Coloureds, so a property test was not the regime's principle.

domination-women-nature.rationale: Inferred: Afrikaner nationalist and Christian-national ideology held conservative gender roles and treated nature as given for human use, so it would reject this claim.

reification.rationale: Inferred: apartheid thought was anti-communist and Christian-national, and rejected Marxist analysis of markets.

press-owned-by-wealth.rationale: Inferred: the regime censored the press and restricted assembly itself, and its anti-communist ideology rejected this Marxist critique.

promulgated-standing-laws.rationale: Apartheid ruled through statute but also through broad executive powers, detention without trial and banning orders, so rule by discretion was central to the security state.

racial-franchise.rationale: Apartheid kept political power with the white minority, and the Verwoerd doctrine confined each group's political rights to its own area or homeland.

online-participation.rationale: Anachronistic: the system ended before the internet reached the public, so there is no stated position.

open-government-data.rationale: Inferred: the security state kept records secret, censored information and restricted press reporting.

interfaith-marriage-restriction.rationale: Inferred: the law banned marriage across racial lines, not across religions; Dutch Reformed leaders discouraged interfaith marriage but the state imposed no ban.

boycott-minority-shops.rationale: Inferred: the state enforced racial separation in trade and residence, but a boycott by religion was not part of the doctrine.

citizens-assembly.rationale: Apartheid placed decision-making in an elected white parliament under guardianship and denied Black South Africans political rights; inferred that a lot-chosen assembly was not part of it.

reinterpret-religion.rationale: Verwoerd and the Dutch Reformed churches defended separate development as scriptural and Calvinist orthodoxy; inferred that updating inherited doctrine was not the stated line.

wealth-concentration-endangers-liberty.rationale: Inferred: the system protected a white-owned economy and was strongly anti-communist, and it did not treat large fortunes as a threat to liberty.

open-lgbt-military-service.rationale: Inferred from the Christian-national moral order claimed in the sources; the state policed morality and a typical adherent would reject open service.

state-promotes-atheism.rationale: The state claimed Christian grounds and was fiercely anti-communist, so promoting unbelief was opposed.

abolish-police-prisons.rationale: Apartheid depended on a large police and security apparatus to enforce its laws, so abolishing it was the opposite of the aim.

power-sharing-divided-societies.rationale: Inferred: it rejected majority rule but wanted separate group rights, with white guardianship, not shared executive power across communities.

charity-over-state-aid.rationale: Inferred: the state ran extensive welfare for whites, so it did not leave poor relief mainly to charity.

term-limits.rationale: Inferred: the sources do not address term limits, and National Party prime ministers served long terms in a dominant-party system.

vote-delegation.rationale: Inferred: political rights were exercised by group and by guardians, not by flexible delegation of votes by each citizen.

existential-risk-priority.rationale: Inferred: the sources never address extinction risk and nothing in the doctrine bears on it.

women-in-religious-leadership.rationale: Inferred from the Christian-national churches that backed the system, which kept clerical office to men.

shared-marital-authority.rationale: Inferred from the patriarchal Christian-national outlook; the husband was head of the household in the law of the time.

foreign-residents-local-vote.rationale: The system denied even South African citizens of the wrong race political rights, so it would not have extended votes to foreign residents.

rent-control.rationale: Inferred: apartheid did not address rent caps as such, though the state set housing and rent in segregated townships; its defenders would split.

abolish-ip.rationale: Inferred: a state-driven nationalist order saw no place for abolishing intellectual property, which it never addressed.

uniformed-youth.rationale: Inferred: Afrikaner nationalist institutions such as the Voortrekkers drilled youth into national service, and the state later ran cadet training in schools.

no-nuclear-weapons-on-territory.rationale: South Africa secretly developed its own nuclear weapons while under apartheid; inferred as a policy of keeping them on its own territory.

no-foreign-bases.rationale: Inferred: the regime guarded South African sovereignty and ended foreign base arrangements, treating outside military presence as interference.

recognise-genocide.rationale: Inferred: the regime denied racial injustice against Black South Africans and would not have accepted such labels; adherents did not address it.

income-for-work-not-ownership.rationale: Apartheid defended property and white capital but reserved skilled jobs for white workers, so its supporters were split on reward for work versus ownership.

never-kill-self-defence.rationale: Inferred: the regime maintained armed police and military forces and justified violence to defend the order and the white minority.

unbroken-national-continuity.rationale: Afrikaner nationalism told of a people with a God-given calling from the 1652 settlement, though it did not claim ancient origins; inferred from Verwoerd's thought.

sex-socially-constructed.rationale: Inferred: apartheid's Calvinist, traditionalist outlook took sex and gender roles as natural and fixed.

no-fixed-category-of-women.rationale: Inferred: the doctrine held fixed categories, including of race and sex, as the basis of the social order.

martyrs-honoured.rationale: Inferred: Afrikaner nationalism honoured its heroes and the dead of the Great Trek and the wars, as in the Day of the Vow.

politics-spiritual-struggle.rationale: Apartheid claimed Christian grounds and framed communism as a total onslaught, so politics was cast as a moral and religious struggle.

homeland-cultural-centre.rationale: The homeland policy aimed to gather each people in its own territory rather than to keep a dispersed diaspora as a cultural centre; inferred.

culture-before-state.rationale: Afrikaner cultural organisations came before the state, but apartheid itself was a state-first project, so adherents would be split; inferred.

god-not-male.rationale: Inferred: the Dutch Reformed churches that backed apartheid taught a male-language God.

scripture-judged-by-women.rationale: Inferred: the Calvinist tradition behind apartheid did not judge texts by women's humanity.

economy-in-majority-hands.rationale: Under apartheid the economy stayed in a white minority's hands, not a national majority's, though Afrikaner economic nationalism also promoted Afrikaners over others; inferred.

single-unit-for-people.rationale: The homeland policy consolidated land for each African people into a single territorial unit, such as Bophuthatswana and Transkei.

independent-unions.rationale: Apartheid law restricted black unions and tightly controlled the labour movement along racial lines.

socialism-needs-workers-power.rationale: The regime was fiercely anti-communist and rejected socialism, so it would reject the claim's premise.

local-essentials-public.rationale: Local services were provided on a segregated basis and not addressed as a principle of ownership.

second-chamber.rationale: The regime had changing chambers (the 1983 tricameral parliament) but no principled position.

municipal-property.rationale: Inferred: the order rested on private property and a state that allocated land by race.

confederal-coordination.rationale: Inferred: separate development gave final authority to the white central government, not to assemblies or confederations.

family-wage.rationale: Inferred: apartheid held black wages low through migrant labour and pay controls, not family-support wages.

anonymous-payments.rationale: Inferred from the security state and censorship, which opposed untraceable activity.

online-anonymity.rationale: Anachronistic; inferred from the security state's surveillance and censorship.

person-over-state.rationale: Verwoerd placed rights within the volk and its guardianship, subordinating the individual to the group and state.

spiritual-nature.rationale: Verwoerd's thought rested on Christian grounds and claimed a spiritual calling for each volk.

regional-powers-revocable.rationale: Homeland self-government was granted by and revocable by the white parliament, which stayed sovereign.

dense-cities.rationale: Inferred: Group Areas and removals kept groups apart and pushed black people out of white urban areas.

racial-group-interests.rationale: Verwoerd's axioms treat each people as a distinct group with its own interests, organised and defended separately.

racial-pride.rationale: Afrikaner nationalism and separate development valued each volk's identity and pride in it.

defensive-wars-only.rationale: The regime framed its military as defending against communism and 'total onslaught', though it also fought abroad.

missingStatements.text: Citizens of different racial groups should have separate political rights and representation.
missingStatements.rationale: Black South Africans lost parliamentary representation and were to exercise political rights only in their homelands, per Verwoerd's policy.

missingStatements.text: Schools should be organised separately for each racial or ethnic group to prepare its pupils for their own community.
missingStatements.rationale: Bantu Education was built to serve each group's own community, and Verwoerd said Black pupils should not be led toward European society.

missingStatements.text: Citizens of a country may be stripped of its citizenship and made citizens of a separate ethnic territory.
missingStatements.rationale: The homeland policy made Black South Africans citizens of homelands, including the four declared independent.
missingStatements.declined: Too specific to apartheid homeland policy; ethnic-nation and racial-segregation-law already separate its defining positions, and few other ideologies would take a side.

notes: Statements outside race, security, communism and nation are mostly inferred (low). Verwoerd's primary words are cited as quoted by Venter and in Hansard, not from original speech texts. Reformist later factions and verligte Afrikaners differed on petty apartheid.
